title: Detect a Cycle (Floyd's Tortoise & Hare)
hints: Move one pointer by one step and another by two; if they ever meet (by `===`), there's a cycle.
To find the start, reset one pointer to the head and advance both one step at a time.
Break the cycle before returning so ARC can deallocate the nodes.
jsBridge: Floyd's tortoise and hare, comparing nodes with `===` (identity). A cyclic list is also a **retain cycle** under ARC, so without breaking it the nodes leak, which JS's GC would clean up.

compass.q: JS's GC frees an unreachable cyclic list. What happens under ARC?
Floyd's O(1) space vs a `Set<ObjectIdentifier>` of visited nodes: which is easier to explain?
Why `===` and not `==` for comparing nodes?
How would you make a cyclic data structure that doesn't leak (weak/unowned back-links)?
